cards.definition: The book's design principle: one theoretical concept (linear independence), one computational tool (QR factorization), and one method family (least squares and extensions) are enough to cover vectors, matrices, and a wide span of applications — data fitting, classification, control, and finance.

Part I frames vectors as the universal container for real-world data: word counts in a document, time series, patient attributes, product sales, audio tracks, images, investment portfolios. Operations (addition, inner product, norm, distance, angle) become data operations.

Part II treats matrices as linear (and affine) functions with concrete instances: geometric transforms, selectors, incidence matrices of graphs, and convolution. QR factorization is introduced as the single computational workhorse; inverses culminate in the pseudo-inverse.

Part III: approximately solving overdetermined systems by minimizing the squared residual. One idea yields data fitting (with validation and feature engineering), binary and multi-class classification, multi-objective and constrained variants, and nonlinear extensions via Gauss-Newton and Levenberg-Marquardt.

Chapters 15-17 extend plain least squares with multiple objectives, linear constraints, and regularization terms — the same machinery behind ridge-style fitting, portfolio optimization, linear quadratic control, and linear quadratic state estimation.

The PDF is legally free because Cambridge University Press allows the authors to host it. The companion page adds lecture slides, lecture videos, a Julia companion, and extra exercises; community Python/Julia notebooks exist. Always link the author's page; never re-host the PDF.

license_note: Copyright held by Cambridge University Press; authors permitted to host the PDF free on the web. Link, do not re-host.
notes: Foundations module, not frontier-core: VMLS is prerequisite mathematics for the frontier AI material elsewhere in IL-23. Companion anchors on the site: the flagship math-for-ml sequence (Gallier manuscript, Strang 18.065). The book assumes no probability/statistics background and only light calculus; programming exercises are encouraged but optional.
objectives: Explain the book's 'intellectual economy': linear independence, QR factorization, and least squares as the three load-bearing ideas
Map the three parts of VMLS (vectors, matrices, least squares) to concrete ML/data-engineering tasks
Use least squares as the unifying method for data fitting, classification, and regularized estimation
Identify which advanced topics (portfolio optimization, LQ control, nonlinear LS) are extensions of the same core method
Locate the free PDF, lecture slides/videos, and Julia/Python companions for self-study

quiz.answer: Linear independence (the one theoretical concept), QR factorization (the one computational tool), and least squares plus its extensions (the one method family).
quiz.question: What are the three load-bearing ideas in VMLS's 'intellectual economy'?

quiz.answer: Any three of: word counts in a document, time series, patient attributes, product sales, audio tracks, images, investment portfolios.
quiz.question: Give three real-world data types the book represents as vectors.

quiz.answer: Because the single idea of minimizing the squared residual of an overdetermined system extends to data fitting, classification, multi-objective and constrained problems, portfolio optimization, control, estimation, and nonlinear model fitting.
quiz.question: Why is least squares described as the book's 'payoff'?

quiz.answer: The Gauss-Newton algorithm and the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm.
quiz.question: Which two algorithms does the book present for nonlinear least squares?

quiz.answer: Familiarity with basic mathematical notation; light calculus appears in a few places but is not a strict prerequisite. No probability or statistics background is needed, and no programming knowledge is required (though computational exercises are encouraged).
quiz.question: What background does the book require, and what does it explicitly not require?
